note: Q63 governs the DA params floors and the owner-set drain protection accepted in F04 §4, and pins them in both languages. Acceptance clauses (a) governed lower bounds and (b) owner-set drain protection are implemented in `onchain/aiken/validators/da-params-governor.ak` and measured by the groups below. Acceptance clause (c) — the partial-attestation rescue/refund path — was delivered later, under the Q62 lane that held the `onchain/aiken/lib/midgard/da-attestation-types.ak` lease, and its two groups are now measured rather than OPEN. The rescue adds a `RescueStrandedAttestation` mint constructor and a `BurnForRescue` spend constructor. Its authorization is a state condition and nothing else — no deadline, no quorum of its own, no new F04 value — and that condition is the exact complement of what `ApplyToStateQueue` requires: the attestation's pinned `committee_signers_hash` OR its pinned `da_threshold` must no longer equal the current authenticated DA params' governed value. An attestation freezes both at Init and apply demands both still match, so it is unrecoverable precisely when either has moved. Taking only the committee half — which the first draft did, and an adversarial review caught before commit — would have left a second silent strand, since the governor permits a threshold change over an unchanged committee: such an attestation could never apply and never be rescued, while `AddSignatures` kept accepting signatures that could never amount to anything, and its ADA would be locked for good. The complement is also not too permissive: whenever it holds the apply gate is unsatisfiable no matter how many further signatures are gathered, so the path can never take value from an attestation still in flight. Rescuable and appliable are complements, never both, and Q62's `strandedness-completeness` group measures that against the same attestation and governed params its apply rejection uses. The refund is bound to the attestation's own value less the burnt DAAT, and the burn is required to be the sole movement of that policy's tokens in the transaction, which is what the duplicate and cross-attestation rejections are derived from. No count here is a declaration count: every published number is recomputed from an executed runner report. Deployment consequence of the F04 §4 floor as amended by the 2026-08-11 owner ruling 4 and the 2026-08-13 in-session owner ruling recorded on #602, written down so it is not rediscovered in the field. The retired `max(2, ceil(2n/3))` clamp made a one-member DA committee unrepresentable; the amended `ceil(2n/3)` floor makes it representable again — `ceil(2*1/3) == 1` — so a committee of one attesting 1-of-1 is admitted. The floor differs from the retired form at exactly one set size, n = 1; for every n >= 2 the two-thirds ceiling is already >= 2, so no other size moved. The 2026-08-13 ruling then dropped the governor's owner-set minimum to one, so a lone owner is admitted too and can rotate the committee and both governed thresholds on its own signature. Single-key governance is therefore ACCEPTED behaviour by owner decision, not an oversight, and is pinned positively by the `single-owner-governance-consequence` group rather than left to be inferred from the absence of a rejection. A fully single-key deployment now bootstraps end to end, emitting one explanatory warning for single-key attestation and one for single-key governance. What no ruling licensed, and what still refuses: an owner set of zero, a threshold of zero at any set size (the floor is >= 1 everywhere), a threshold above its own set size, and any malformed or unsorted set encoding.

compiler.rule: Aiken test execution for this goal is fork-only: the stock v1.1.22 build that is the authority for compilation and applied validator hashes ships a codegen defect and takes hours over this tree, so it is used only for `aiken check --skip-tests`. The gate resolves the compiler from `MIDGARD_AIKEN_BIN` then `MIDGARD_FORK_AIKEN_BIN` (CI pins only the latter) and fails closed with ERR_AIKEN_BINARY_UNPINNED when neither is set, rather than falling through to whatever `aiken` is first on PATH. Whichever resolves must then report a `aiken v1.1.23` version or the run fails closed with ERR_AIKEN_COMPILER_MISMATCH, so a stock binary cannot supply a result under the fork's name. Both behaviours are seeded self-tests, not assurances: the gate spawns itself with the variables stripped, and again against a stub binary reporting a v1.1.22 version.

implementation.constantSplit: Both governed constants that once sat beside the floor are retired, by two owner rulings. `min_governed_threshold` / `MIN_DA_GOVERNED_THRESHOLD` bounded a threshold and went with the 2026-08-11 clamp retirement. `min_owner_count` bounded a set size and went with the 2026-08-13 owner ruling that dropped the owner-set minimum to one: at one it would have been a guard that cannot fail, because `sorted_unique_len_at_most` opens with `expect [first, ..rest] = keys` and aborts on an empty set before a count exists to compare, so the validator declares no such constant and the non-emptiness refusal is structural. It is measured directly by `da_params_governor_rejects_empty_owner_set` rather than left resting on that argument. Off-chain `MIN_DA_OWNER_COUNT` survives at 1 because the check there is genuinely not vacuous: `daParamsFloorViolations` takes `ownerCount` as caller-supplied data and a caller can pass zero, so it still reports its own `owner_set_below_minimum` class. A review finding then gave it a committee-side twin, `MIN_DA_COMMITTEE_SIZE` at 1, for the same reason and for diagnostic parity: `committeeLength` is caller-supplied too, and over an empty committee the threshold bounds alone say nothing — `governedThresholdFloor(0) === 0`, so a zero threshold sits on that floor and does not exceed the empty committee either — which had left an empty committee reported as no violation at all. It reports `committee_below_minimum`, and a swept control pins that it fires at no other committee size, so no previously reported result moved. Neither off-chain constant is a governed bound the validator lacks; both are diagnostics over caller-supplied counts for refusals the validator makes structurally. The floor itself is a function of set size alone, and on-chain no constant sits beside it.

groups.claim: The floor arithmetic the governor applies reproduces the F04 majority DA floor, the same two-thirds ceiling over the owner set, and what the owner-set drain protection still rests on after both owner rulings: a floor that never returns less than one at any set size, so no set — however small — can name a threshold of zero. It rests on no governed constant any more; both were retired with the rulings, and the empty owner set is a datum disposition rather than arithmetic, measured by `below-floor-drain-rejections`.

groups.claim: The mint handler itself enforces the governed floors on the params output it authorises, so the governor cannot be initialised with below-floor params.
groups.languageRationale: On-chain only by construction, and declared so. The claim is about a Plutus minting policy resolving the output it authorises; the SDK builds no DA-params initialisation transaction, so there is no off-chain twin that could carry this cardinality. This is the seam that binds the governed floors to the params a deployment is *initialised* with rather than only to the ones a later update continues, which is why it is measured separately from the spend seam. Since both owner rulings it is no longer where single-key configurations are refused — a one-member committee and a one-owner set are both mintable, and the node's single-key defaults initialise with warnings — so what it refuses, and what the pair below measures, is an initial datum below the governed floors.

groups.claim: The spend handler itself enforces the governed floors on the continuing output, so a quorum cannot rotate the params into a below-floor configuration.
groups.languageRationale: On-chain only by construction, and declared so rather than left to be inferred from the citation list. The claim is about a Plutus spending handler resolving its own continuing output; the SDK builds no DA-params update transaction, so there is no off-chain twin that could carry this cardinality. Every other measured group is required to carry it in both languages.

groups.claim: The off-chain floor reproduces the F04 arithmetic over every representable set size, measured against a digest the verifier recomputes independently rather than against the quoted decision text.
groups.languageRationale: Off-chain only by construction, and declared so. The verifier is a Node process: it can import no Aiken. The two sides are therefore measured to different depths, and the difference is deliberate rather than glossed: full-table off-chain (this group sweeps 0..max_indexed_signer_count and pins the digest), sample-pinned on-chain (`da_params_governor_invariant_da_threshold_majority_floor` pins a sample of set sizes that straddles the clamp boundary and reaches the top of the range at 100, 255 and 256). No full-table on-chain claim is made anywhere, because no full-table Aiken sweep exists.

titles: provenance — the SDK floor reproduces the F04 arithmetic over every representable set size

groups.claim: A partially signed attestation stranded by a mid-flight committee rotation can be rescued/refunded.
groups.languageRationale: On-chain only by construction, and declared so rather than left to be inferred from an absent citation. The claim is that a Plutus policy releases a stranded UTxO's value, which is settled only by running the `da_attestation` mint and spend handlers against a transaction; a Node verifier can execute no Plutus. The control therefore carries both handlers, because a rescue transaction is valid only if both run — the mint half decides whether the attestation is stranded and where its value goes, the spend half binds that particular UTxO to the decision, and pinning only the mint would leave the binding the replay rejection attacks unmeasured. The off-chain half of this work exists and is measured, but under Q62's gate and against different claims (redeemer ABI ordering, and the builder's refusal to rescue a live attestation), so it is not cited here as if it carried this cardinality.

groups.claim: The rescue path rejects theft of another party's attestation value, duplicate refunds, and replay of a consumed rescue.
groups.languageRationale: On-chain only, for the same reason as the rescue path itself: each rejection is a Plutus handler refusing a transaction. Each is also a one-field mutation of the control's transaction, which is why they are measured against the same fixture rather than restated off-chain. Theft is the state-condition negative — the governed committee still equals the one the attestation froze, so the attestation is in flight and its value is not the rescuer's to take; without that condition the path would be a burn-and-take backdoor over every live attestation. Duplicate is the burn-quantity negative: because this policy is stateless it cannot prove per-header uniqueness, so two DAAT UTxOs may share an asset name, and retiring both under one authorization collapses to exactly the `-2` the sole-burn check refuses. Replay is the binding negative: the rescue mint redeemer names one input, so its authorization cannot be replayed onto a second attestation UTxO bundled into the same transaction.

WITHDRAWN by the 2026-08-13 Option-B ruling, and recorded rather than deleted because it pointed the opposite way. This entry used to ask the parent to move `demo/midgard-node/src/transactions/initialization.ts` off its single-key DA defaults — `owners: [operatorKeyHash]`, `update_threshold: 1n`, `DA_THRESHOLD` defaulting over a one-member committee — on the ground that F04 §4 forbade that shape and the governor would not mint it. Both rulings retired that ground: the committee floor at n = 1 is one, the governor declares no owner-set minimum, and the whole configuration is mintable. The node keeps it and emits one explanatory warning per single-key side instead of refusing, which is delivered here rather than owed. The parent owes no correction, and must not reinstate a `>= 2-of-N` requirement in this path: doing so would refuse what the owner accepted.

Likewise withdrawn as a blanket correction. Suites outside this task's lease pin `update_threshold: 1n` or a single-key committee — `demo/midgard-node/tests/initialization-emulator.test.ts`, `demo/midgard-sdk/tests/da-attestation.test.ts`, `demo/da-committee-node/tests/startup-da-params.test.ts`, `demo/da-committee-node/tests/scalus-add-signatures-eval.test.ts`, `demo/da-committee-node/tests/da-attestation-reader.test.ts` — and pinning either is no longer a defect in itself. What the parent must check per fixture is the governed bounds that survive, which are set-relative rather than absolute: `update_threshold: 1n` is valid exactly over an owner set of one and below floor over any larger set, and `da_threshold` must still sit at or above `ceil(2*committee_len/3)` and no higher than the committee. Only the fixtures that violate one of those still need correction.
